vocabulary.meaning_en: 1) more than you want or need (usually negative); 2) also
vocabulary.note_ar: حيلة: too فيها حرفا o، أي أكثر من اللازم
vocabulary.note_en: Trick: "too" has one o too many – more than needed.
vocabulary.example: It's too hot to go out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: 1) very, to a great extent (usually positive); 2) therefore; 3) in "I think so"
vocabulary.note_ar: حيلة: S مثل smile (ابتسامة) أي إيجابي غالبًا
vocabulary.note_en: Trick: S for smile – usually positive.
vocabulary.example: The soup was so good, I asked for a second bowl.

vocabulary.meaning_en: more than is needed or allowed
vocabulary.example: Fifty degrees is an excessive heat for me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: permitted; that you are allowed to do
vocabulary.example: Two bags is the allowable amount.

vocabulary.meaning_en: how much, how far; a measurement of degree
vocabulary.example: "So" shows the extent: so quickly, so quietly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: special strength given to a word or idea
a word that joins two ideas: and, but, so

vocabulary.example: It was late; therefore, we went home.
The road was closed; thus, we were late.
She moved so quietly, nobody noticed.

fine_lines.title: too hot vs so hot
fine_lines.explanation_ar: too = تجاوز الحد، أكثر من المقبول، وغالبًا سلبي (لا أستطيع). so = درجة عالية جدًا لكن ضمن الحد، وغالبًا إيجابي أو للتوكيد. The soup was too hot = لم أستطع أكله. The soup was so hot = كان ساخنًا جدًا فانتظرت قليلًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Too" = past the limit, more than is OK, usually negative (I can't). "So" = a very high degree but not past the limit, often positive or for emphasis. "The soup was too hot" = I couldn't eat it. "The soup was so hot" = very hot, so I waited a little.

examples.sentence: It's too hot in Riyadh for me in summer.
The soup was so good, I asked for more.

fine_lines.title: too (excessive) vs too (also)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: too قبل الصفة أو الظرف = أكثر من اللازم. too في آخر الجملة = أيضًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Too" before an adjective/adverb = more than needed. "Too" at the end = also.

examples.sentence: He went, and I went, too.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite thank-you: you are very kind (positive "too").
expressions.example: "I brought you some coffee." "You're too kind!"

expressions.meaning_en: A polite reply when someone gives you something.
expressions.example: "Would you like my seat?" "Oh, you're too generous."

expressions.phrase: I think so. / I thought so.
expressions.example: "Did he bring the book?" "I think so."

grammar.title: too = excessive (usually negative)
grammar.explanation_ar: too قبل صفة أو ظرف يعني أكثر مما تريد أو تحتاج أو مما هو مسموح، وعادة تكون النتيجة سلبية.
grammar.explanation_en: "Too" before an adjective or adverb means more than you want, need or is allowed, usually with a negative result.
examples: James usually talks too fast, so I don't understand him.
It's too hot for me there.

grammar.title: too can be positive (polite phrases)
grammar.explanation_ar: في عبارات قليلة مثل You're too kind و You're too generous تكون too إيجابية وتعني "جدًا".
grammar.explanation_en: In a few polite phrases like "You're too kind" and "You're too generous", "too" is positive and means "very".

grammar.title: too = also (at the end)
grammar.explanation_ar: too في آخر الجملة تعني "أيضًا" وتأتي بعد مفعول أو فعل.
grammar.explanation_en: "Too" at the end of a sentence means "also"; it can follow an object or a verb.
examples: Mr. E likes cake, and I like it, too.
He went, and I went, too.

grammar.title: so = extent and emphasis
grammar.explanation_ar: so ظرف يبين الدرجة (كم؟) ويعطي توكيدًا، ويأتي بعده غالبًا نتيجة: so quickly (that) it's hard to understand.
grammar.explanation_en: "So" is an adverb of extent (how much?) and emphasis, often followed by a result: so quickly (that) it's hard to understand.
examples: He speaks so quickly, it's hard to understand him.
She moved so quietly, nobody noticed.

grammar.title: so = conjunction (therefore) and truth (I think so)
grammar.explanation_ar: so أداة ربط بمعنى "لذلك" (therefore / thus). وتُستعمل أيضًا في I think so / I thought so بمعنى أظن أنه صحيح. too لا تملك هذين المعنيين.
grammar.explanation_en: "So" is a conjunction meaning "therefore" (thus). It is also used in "I think so / I thought so" = I believe it's true. "Too" has neither of these meanings.
examples: I wasn't feeling well, so I went to the doctor.
It was cold out, so I got my jacket.

questions.question: "James talks ___ fast, so I don't understand him."
questions.explanation_ar: أكثر من اللازم بنتيجة سلبية: too.
questions.explanation_en: More than OK, with a negative result: too.

questions.question: "The soup was ___ good, I asked for a second bowl."
"It was cold out, ___ I got my jacket."
"Mr. E likes cake, and I like it, ___."
"Would you like my seat?" "Thank you, you're ___ kind."
questions.explanation_ar: You're too kind عبارة مهذبة إيجابية.
questions.explanation_en: "You're too kind" is a polite, positive phrase.

questions.question: "Did he bring the book?" "I think ___."
questions.explanation_en: "I think so" = I believe it's true.

questions.question: "This box is ___ heavy. I can't lift it."
questions.explanation_en: Past the limit, I can't: too.

questions.question: "She moved ___ quietly, nobody noticed."
questions.explanation_en: A high degree with a result: so.
